title: AVERAGE vs AVERAGEIF vs AVERAGEIFS
description: Learn when to use AVERAGE, AVERAGEIF, and AVERAGEIFS for different averaging needs.
intro: AVERAGE calculates the mean of all values. AVERAGEIF averages values that meet one condition. AVERAGEIFS averages values that meet multiple conditions.
whenToUseA: Use AVERAGE when you want the mean of all numeric values in a range.
whenToUseB: Use AVERAGEIF when you need to filter by one condition, such as averaging scores for a single class.
whenToUseC: Use AVERAGEIFS when you need to filter by two or more conditions.
verdict: Start with AVERAGE for simple means. Use AVERAGEIF or AVERAGEIFS when you need conditional averages.

faq.question: Does AVERAGEIF ignore blanks?
faq.answer: Yes, blanks in the average_range are ignored.

faq.question: Can AVERAGEIFS use OR logic?
faq.answer: No, it uses AND logic. Add multiple AVERAGEIFS for OR logic.
